title: Attestation Mode — Who Proved the Authorization
note: The most consequential field in the envelope. `PrincipalSigned` means the human's own key signed this envelope and `proof` is a two-element chain. `NotaryAttested` — which is also what an ABSENT field means — means the signature is a notary asserting that a human agreed, which is a strictly weaker claim. A verifier whose policy requires `PrincipalSigned` MUST refuse the weaker mode rather than silently accept it, for the same reason §8.4.6 forbids downgrading key discovery: an attacker who can defeat the weak path will always present the weak path. `delegation_mandate` embeds the full parent grant because `delegation_mandate_id` is an id, and an id proves nothing — embedding makes the human's signature, the granted scope, and the window all checkable offline, provided the verifier also binds the mandate to THIS envelope by comparing `human_principal_did` and `agent_did` (§7.1.7.1). The values are declared as the `Vocabulary::AttestationMode` enum; the prop stays `str` because the wire carries a bare string, not a tagged object.
book_ref: APH Spec: §7.1.7 PolicyDescriptor, §7.1.7.1 Why the delegation is embedded, §8.3.1 Verifying a proof chain
